title: Ampleness restricts to closed subschemes
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $M$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every closed immersion $i:X\to Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], the pullback $i^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is ample on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 01PU (lemma-ample-on-closed): restriction of an ample invertible sheaf to any closed subscheme is ample.

proof.text: Put $L=i^*M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], $L$ is invertible. Ampleness of $M$ implies that $Y$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The definition of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies $X$ homeomorphically with the closed subset $i(X)$ of $Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact] to that closed subset. Thus $X$ is quasi-compact.

Fix $x\in X$. By ampleness [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], choose $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ such that $i(x)\in Y_s$ and $Y_s$ is affine. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-power-section-nonvanishing-pullback] to the morphism $i$, the invertible module $M$, this positive integer $n$ and the section $s$. It gives a global section $t\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$ whose nonvanishing open is $X_t=i^{-1}(Y_s)$. In particular $x\in X_t$.

Since $i$ is a closed immersion and $Y_s$ is an affine open, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] says that $i^{-1}(Y_s)$ is affine. Hence the section $t$ of Step 2 has affine nonvanishing open $X_t$ containing $x$. For every $x$ we have now produced the positive tensor-power section required by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Together with invertibility and quasi-compactness from Step 1, this is ampleness of $L=i^*M$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q86-b10c4dc88 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and every node it cites in full. The statement matches Stacks properties.tex Tag 01PU (lemma-ample-on-closed, l.4274) with Definition 01PS (l.4243) exactly: Y is any scheme, M is ample and invertible, i is any closed immersion, and the claim is that i^*M is ample. No hypothesis is added or dropped. Step 1 shows i^*M is invertible (lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible, sorry-free in slopmaster2). It then uses that Y is quasi-compact by the definition of ampleness, that i is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, and IsClosed.isCompact (Topology 005C), so X is quasi-compact. Step 2 takes n>=1 and s with i(x) in Y_s and Y_s affine. lem-weil-pbc-tensor-power-section-nonvanishing-pullback (sorry-free in slopmaster2) then gives a section t of the n-th power of the pullback with X_t = i^{-1}(Y_s), using the same nonvanishing predicate, so this is a real section transport and not just an isomorphism. Step 3 uses clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion, a Mathlib leaf for Stacks 01QO/01IH, to show X_t is affine, which completes the definition. All cited statements are Mathlib leaves or sorry-free in slopmaster2, so nothing leaves the unit's route and no tool_uses entry is needed. The parent unit's Step 3 uses the item with matching hypotheses. I checked these cases: X empty, i the identity, Spec R/I inside Spec R, and non-reduced X or I not of finite type. There are no new nodes, no cycles and no SGA citations; Mathlib searches are recorded honestly, with LeanSearch marked unavailable.
